L150: 
L151: Every person has a right to access public information. This is established in The Massachusetts Public Records Law (M.G.L. Chapter 66 & Chapter 4, Section 7(26)).
L152: 
L153: In order to assist members of the public with accessing public records in the custody of the Office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth (Office), the following guidelines are provided.
L154: The Office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth has custody of certain public records. To assist members of the public, we provide the following guidelines. Requests for public records should be directed to the Office's Records Access Officer. The Records Access Officer can be contacted at:
L155: 
L156: Sofya Gray
L157: Records Access Officer
L158: cite71†Office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth One Ashburton Place - Room 1711 Boston, MA 02108†www.google.com L159: Phone: 617-878-3660
L160: Fax: 617-742-4538
L161: Email: Sec.RAO@sec.state.ma.us
L162: It’s best to submit a public records request in writing. This ensures the Office accurately and completely responds to your request.
L163: 
L164: A request for public records should include a reasonable description of specific records being requested.
L165: 
L166: The Office can assess a reasonable fee for the production of public records.
L167: 
L168: The public records maintained by the Office include, but are not limited to, records contained within the following areas of the Office:
L169:   * Public Records Division
L170:   * Elections Division
L171:   * Corporations Division
L172:   * Securities Division
L173:   * Lobbyist Division
L174:   * Massachusetts Archives
L175:   * Massachusetts Historical Commission
L176:   * State Publications and Regulations Division
L177: 
L178: Requests for land records from Registries of Deeds should be made directly to the applicable Registry. cite72†Information pertaining to the Registries can be found here. L179: The Public Records Division of the Secretary of the Commonwealth’s Office maintains a cite73†searchable website of public records requests that have been received and reported by other state agencies. Requests for records from state agencies outside the Secretary of the Commonwealth’s Office should be submitted directly to the appropriate agency. The Secretary’s office does not have custody of the records of other agencies.
